newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares drift lower on political worries.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares drift lower on political worries.

text.p: Delhi shares opened lower in volatile trade on Tuesday on institutional selling triggered by adverse political developments, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 8.14 points lower at 899.12 after 30 minutes of trade.
"Adverse political conditions triggered selling and forced overseas investors to withdraw their buying support for the time being," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Services.

Traders said newspaper reports that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram has warned the leftist allies in the ruling United Front coalition to refrain from pressurising the decision making Steering Committee to enforce their agenda, created uneasiness in the market.
The Economic Times newspaper quoted Chidambaram asking the Communist Party of India (Marxist) not to impose their agenda on the ruling coalition.
"Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) ministers will quit their posts if they are not allowed to fulfill their tasks," Chidambaram said.
Chidambaram's TMC is a key constitutient of the 15-party coalition government.
Reliance Industries slipped 5.75 rupees lower at 366.50.
State Bank of India fell 4.45 rupees to 319.50.
Larsen and Toubro decreased 3.40 rupees to 269.00.
